title: Price monomial guard headers with sharp ternary row-addition budgets (no κ)
body:
## Result

How much coordinate mixing is needed when permutations and nonzero scalings are free, and each elementary row addition costs one? This follows the monomial-header question in [PR #6710](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6710), pinned at `465a0060fbd236a5e202619de4a45a694d44970a`.

- The exact price of separating a full affine family's slopes is **h − Z**, with h nonzero vector charges and Z the maximum number of disjoint zero-sum blocks. An anchored scalar carrier makes this the full proper-minor price as well. For arbitrary binary normalized guard lists the exact full price has the same form after adjoining one dummy charge. [Proof and witnesses](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/PROOF.md)
- For any ternary full flat, let S and L be its separate slope and scalar-imbalance prices. The true price lies between **max(S,L) and 2S+L**. Both endpoints are attained at every prescribed pair of nonnegative values S,L across dimensions. Even S+L can underestimate the cost by an arbitrarily large amount in a single pencil. [Sharp price bounds](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/GAP.md)
- Two five-element pencils with four active charges need **two versus three** row additions. All states at smaller cost fail a literal minor check under every final permutation. The variable-prime anchored decision problem is strongly NP-complete via 3-PARTITION. For fixed small alphabets we give constructive algorithms and scalar closed forms. [Algorithms](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/ALGORITHM.md) · [Actual shortest examples](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/EXAMPLES.json)
- Over the ternary field, five is the first dimension in which the larger separate bound can be strictly low. Exactly 1,920 labeled five-coordinate pencil tuples have that gap. [Orbit classification](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/ORBITS.md)

The classical monetary debt-partition principle and its complexity are credited to the earlier literature. Here the transfer graph comes from actual inverse dual row operations, with a legal attaining header and checks of the original principal minors. This counts an explicitly scoped header alphabet and does not price the physical caller or change the selected multiplication exponent. [Source pins](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/SOURCES.json) · [Overlap and scope](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91/research/monomial-guard-settlement/OVERLAP.json)

<details><summary>Independent five-coordinate raw-state recount</summary>

The published raw graph also visited all **1,568,160 labeled ternary pencil tuples** at dimension five. It recovered the same full cost histogram and exactly **1,920** strict gaps, without grouping by free orbits. From the package directory, this short replay prints `{0: 1566240, 1: 1920}` up to dictionary order.

```python
from collections import Counter
from flat_oracle import distances_to_passing_pencils
from settlement import Field

states, distance = distances_to_passing_pencils(Field(3), 5)
gaps = Counter()
for state in states:
    u, b, w = state[:5], state[5:10], state[10:]
    x = [a*c % 3 for a, c in zip(u, b)]
    y = [a*c % 3 for a, c in zip(u, w)]
    plus, minus = y.count(1), y.count(2)
    S = plus + minus - min(plus, minus) - abs(plus - minus)//3
    D = x.count(1) - x.count(2)
    L = min(abs(D-1), abs(D+2))//3
    gaps[distance[state] - max(S, L)] += 1
print(dict(gaps))
```
</details>
